title: Consolidated routing decision canonicalization and per-hop metric exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As routing policies grow (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants), downstream services and SRE need a single, compact, canonical record for each routing decision that can be ingested by tracing, logging, and metrics backends. Current state: we emit heterogeneous decision logs across components (router, fallback manager, model-variant-resolver) with differing field names, inconsistent IDs, and duplicated per-hop timing fields. This makes joins, rollups, and SLO calculations error-prone and expensive.

Goal: Define and implement a compact 'routing_provenance' canonical record and export per-hop metrics (latency, queue_time, selected_variant, decision_reason) with stable identifiers so we can reliably attribute latency and errors to specific routing hops and evaluate fallback frequency across regions and tiers.

Success criteria:
- schema doc published and reviewed in Confluence (link below)
- every routing decision emits a single routing_provenance event with stable 32-char hex canonical_id, parent_hop list (as compressed IDs), and a top-level decision_trace_id that maps to a trace/span for distributed tracing
- per-hop metrics available in Prometheus timeseries: routing_hop_latency_ms{hop="region_select"|"tier_route"|"variant_resolve"}, routing_hop_queue_ms, routing_hop_fallback_count
- dashboards: per-model-variant fallback rate, regional fallback heatmap, routing latency SLOs by tier
- end-to-end test in canary environment showing <1% increase in median request latency and accurate attribution in synthetic traffic with forced fallbacks

Technical approach:
1) Canonicalization library: small Go library under infra/routing/canon that takes component-native decision structs and emits the canonical routing_provenance JSON. It will generate canonical_id as stable hash over (request_id, route_config_version, seed) and include a short path of hop IDs. The library will also expose helper functions to attach the decision_trace_id to OpenTelemetry spans.
2) Instrument router, fallback-manager, and variant-resolver to call the canon library at the decision point and emit a single event to the unified routing topic (Kafka) and to local structured logs (JSON) when Kafka is unavailable.
3) Metrics exporter: augment runtime-side Prometheus exporter to increment per-hop counters and observe latency histograms using the same canonical_id as a label (sampled at 1% to avoid cardinality explosion). Use an index label 'hop_id' and 'variant' and tag 'tier' and 'region'.
4) Traces: wire decision_trace_id into OpenTelemetry as a top-level span; add span attributes for canonical_id and hop_name. Sampling defaults to 0.5% for full traces tied to routing decisions but increases to 5% for requests that experienced fallback or error.
5) Backends and retention: Kafka topic retention set to 7 days; routing_provenance events have an event_ttl field. Downstream processors will transform events into the observability warehouse for long-term analysis.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: implement canon library + schema doc; internal review with RT and SRE
- Week 2: instrument router in canary; emit events to staging Kafka; validate schema and sample consumption
- Week 3: instrument fallback-manager and variant-resolver; add Prometheus metrics; enable minimal dashboards
- Week 4: increase sampling on faults; full canary against production traffic subset; run anomaly detection on fallback spikes
- Post-rollout: migrate ad-hoc logs to canonical events and deprecate older event shapes

Telemetry schema reference (high level):
- routing_provenance: {canonical_id, decision_trace_id, request_id, route_config_version, timestamps:{decision_time, enqueue_time}, hops:[{hop_id, hop_name, start_ms, end_ms, reason, selected_variant}], final_outcome, event_ttl}
- metrics: routing_hop_latency_ms (histogram), routing_hop_queue_ms (histogram), routing_hop_fallback_total (counter), routing_decision_errors_total (counter)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Cardinality: including canonical_id as a label in Prometheus is dangerous. Plan: only include canonical_id in a sampled trace subset and use aggregated labels (region, tier, variant) for metrics. We need approval from SRE on sampling limits.
- ID stability: how to derive canonical_id so retries and redirects map to the same route? Proposed deterministic hash including request_id + route_config_version, but epoch migrations may break stability.
- Privacy: canonical_id must not encode PII. Library will strip user-identifiable fields and log only hashed tokens.

Risks:
- Minor latency increase due to canonicalization calls on hot path. Mitigation: micro-optimized hashing and offer a fast-path no-op in environments that disable provenance.
- Metric cardinality explosion. Mitigation: enforce label-only on low-cardinality labels and sampling for high-cardinality ids.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/Canonical+Routing+Provenance
- Schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/schemas/pull/142
- Prototype router PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/396
- Dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/route-provenance/staging

Notes for reviewers: Please review the canonical_id derivation section in the design doc (collision risks and migration plan). SRE: please weigh in on Prometheus sampling thresholds and Kafka retention. Security: confirm no PII is present in canonicalization inputs.
